title: Modules, controllers, and providers
summary: Wire a controller and a provider into a feature module with constructor injection.

scenario.briefing: The campus catalog is being split into feature modules. The products endpoint must be owned by a module instead of constructing its service by hand.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: Add ProductsService to the module providers array.
Declare a constructor parameter typed as ProductsService.
Return this.products.findAll() from the GET handler.
Remove any direct new ProductsService() construction.

misconceptions.description: Creating the service with new inside the controller.
misconceptions.feedback: That bypasses the container. Register the provider and ask for it in the constructor.
misconceptions.testDescription: The controller receives its service through constructor injection.

misconceptions.description: Adding a controller without its provider.
misconceptions.feedback: Nest cannot resolve a constructor dependency that no module provides. Register the provider or import the module that exports it.
misconceptions.testDescription: The service is registered as a provider in the module.

misconceptions.description: Believing new makes a controller easier to test.
misconceptions.feedback: Constructing the service by hand bypasses the injector and hides the dependency from test overrides. Inject it through the constructor.

sections.title: A module is a boundary
sections.body: The module declares which controllers and providers belong to one feature. Nest builds the dependency graph from that declaration instead of from imports buried in the controller.

sections.title: Constructor injection is the seam
sections.body: A controller lists what it needs in its constructor. Nest resolves each parameter from the module's providers, which keeps the controller testable with a substitute.

sections.title: Controllers route, services decide
sections.body: The controller maps HTTP requests to method calls. Business logic belongs in the provider, where it can be reused and tested without an HTTP context.

vocabulary.definition: A class decorated with @Module that groups controllers and providers.
A class registered with Nest so it can be injected into other classes.
Declaring dependencies as constructor parameters and letting the container supply them.

steps.title: Modules and injection

statements.label: A NestJS module declares which controllers and providers belong together.
Nest resolves constructor parameters from providers registered in the module.
A controller should construct its service with new to stay testable.
A provider registered in a module is available to every module without exports.

steps.explanation: The module owns the provider registry, and Nest injects constructor parameters from it. A hand-built service bypasses the container and hides the dependency from tests.
hints: Check each statement against Nest's module provider registry.
Reject the claim that new keeps a controller testable.
Confirm that providers are private to a module unless exported.
Select statements about module boundaries and constructor injection.
